rows.document_title: Paryz, Upgrades at the NASA Langley Research Center National Transonic Facility (AIAA 2012, NASA NTRS 20120001450)
rows.quote: The National Transonic Facility (NTF) is a fan-driven, closed-circuit, continuous-flow cryogenic pressurized wind tunnel that became operational in 1984
rows.reasoning: This key is the controlled cold-side boundary of a guarded insulation calorimeter. NASA's own description says the NTF is a pressurized wind tunnel for aerodynamic model testing. It has no calorimeter and no cold boundary plate, so the function does not exist on this machine. The same paper also gives the whole tunnel gas envelope as -250 F (-157 C, about 116 K) to +150 F, which is far above the 20 K the experiment needs.

rows.quote: The National Transonic Facility (NTF) is a fan-driven, closed-circuit, continuous-flow cryogenic pressurized wind tunnel that became operational in 1984
rows.reasoning: This key is the controlled warm-side boundary of a guarded insulation calorimeter. The NTF is described as a cryogenic pressurized wind tunnel. It has no insulation-calorimeter warm boundary, so the function does not exist. The tunnel's flow temperature range (-250 F to +150 F, about 116 K to 339 K) is a property of the flow, not a calorimeter boundary, so it is not used as this value.

rows.document_title: Paryz, Upgrades at the NASA Langley Research Center National Transonic Facility (AIAA 2012, NASA NTRS 20120001450)
rows.quote: The NTF supports testing of stability and control, cruise performance, stall buffet onset, and configuration aerodynamics.
rows.reasoning: NASA lists what the facility tests, and all of it is aerodynamic model testing on strut or sting supports with strain-gage balances. The introduction calls it a cryogenic pressurized wind tunnel. Guarded heat-flow calorimetry for MLI heat leak is a different kind of instrument, and nothing in the facility description includes it.

rows.document_title: Paryz, Upgrades at the NASA Langley Research Center National Transonic Facility (AIAA 2012, NASA NTRS 20120001450)
rows.location: p. 2, I. Introduction, operating pressure sentence
rows.quote: The facility can operate from 14.7 psia (101.4KPa) to 133 psia (917.0 KPa) (1 to 9 atmospheres; 1.01 to 9.2 bar) in either medium.
rows.reasoning: The test section is the flow circuit of a pressurized tunnel. Its documented operating pressure starts at 1 atmosphere and goes up to 9 atmospheres, so it is never evacuated. This is a stated operating envelope, not silence.
